title: Film record() swallows a failed world read and the beat passes with no figures
body:
## Summary
Under ?take=film the hook's record() catches any failed core read (list_deals, deal_display, deal_groups, deal_history) and returns {}, which is also the shape of 'this beat has no record', so a shop/deadlines/decisions plate ships empty and the capture exits 0.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/director/Director.tsx:522-524 returns {} from the catch of the chapter-record reads; apps/desktop/client/scripts/film-capture.mjs:262-273 only attaches row.record when it has keys, and recordShownOnStage({}) (apps/desktop/client/src/director/takes.ts:734) reports nothing, so a broken read is indistinguishable from a beat without figures. The haggle branch's mandate_list catch (Director.tsx:534-536) is a documented degrade and stays. Fixed: the read returns a marker ({ error }) that film-capture turns into a problem for the row.

## Flow
- film-capture plays shop-prices; deal_groups rejects inside the mock core
- record() catch -> {} ; shown({}) -> []
- the row has no record and no error; the shop plate has no prices; exit 0
- fix: extract the chapter read into a function taking the core's invoke, return { error } on a failed read, film-capture pushes it into problems

## Expected impact
The film's figure plates (shop prices, deadlines, who decided) cannot silently go blank in the hackathon take. Risk: a transient read failure now marks a beat broken.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a failed record read is reported instead of passing as an empty record
Before: 4 chapter kinds (shop, silence, closed, end) read through one catch that yields {}; 0 report a failure (read of Director.tsx:500-525)
After: predicted: a rejecting invoke yields a problem on the row (measured by the instrument)
Method: simulation - the read lives inside the Director component; no unit seam makes it fail in this round
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The film's figure plates (shop prices, deadlines, who decided) cannot silently go blank in the hackathon take. Risk: a transient read failure now marks a beat broken.
instrument: extract readChapterRecord(invoke, world, beat) and a vitest in src/director/film.test.ts with an invoke that rejects for deal_groups: expect { error } (red on today's {}), then film-capture adds it to problems (node --check)

title: A FILM_PRESS target that no longer resolves drops the click ripple silently
body:
## Summary
When a beat's press selector (FILM_PRESS) measures to nothing, the director logs no click and nothing reports it, so the film loses that beat's press ripple and the capture exits 0.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/director/Director.tsx:332-334 sets pressRef to [] when measure(press) is null; apps/desktop/client/scripts/film-capture.mjs:261 reads clicks() and never compares it with what the beat should have pressed. The 4 selectors resolve today (.f.ticker at apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/forms.tsx:141, .puck-art at apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/Puck.tsx:57, .ui-btn.gold from Btn kind gold at apps/desktop/client/src/windows/tumbler/forms.tsx:280), but a Tumbler restyle would drop them without a word. Fixed: the hook says which press target the beat had and whether it was found; film-capture records a problem when a named target was not found.

## Flow
- a Tumbler restyle renames .puck-art
- haggle-card plays: measure(FILM_PRESS[haggle-card]) -> null -> clicks() []
- film-capture writes the row with 0 clicks and no error; exit 0
- fix: FilmHook.press() -> { target, found }; film-capture pushes "press target X not drawn"

## Expected impact
The 4 pressed beats of the hero film keep their ripple or fail loudly. Risk: none beyond a new hook field.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a lost press target is reported
Before: 4 FILM_PRESS beats; 0 report an unresolved target (Director.tsx:332-334, film-capture.mjs:261)
After: predicted 4 of 4 report; measured by the instrument
Method: simulation - the measure runs in a browser frame; the pure seam does not exist yet
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The 4 pressed beats of the hero film keep their ripple or fail loudly. Risk: none beyond a new hook field.
instrument: a pure pressFor(beatId, measure) in takes.ts with a vitest (measure -> null gives { target, found: false }), wired into FilmHook and film-capture problems

title: takes.mjs stops its vite with SIGTERM only; film-capture kills the tree on Windows
body:
## Summary
Two copies of 'start vite, stop it at the end': film-capture.mjs kills the whole process tree with taskkill /T on Windows because vite's children survive otherwise, while scripts/lib/rig.mjs ensureServer (used by takes.mjs) only sends SIGTERM to the node process.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/scripts/lib/rig.mjs:72-75 stop() = child.kill('SIGTERM'); apps/desktop/client/scripts/film-capture.mjs:102-110 stop() runs taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F on win32 with the note "vite's own children too (Windows keeps them otherwise)". The fix was made in one copy only, and film-capture's startServer duplicates ensureServer's ~30 lines. Fixed: one killTree in rig.mjs used by both; film-capture's startServer keeps only its two differences (refuse a busy port, --keep-server).

## Flow
- on Windows: pnpm takes --check (no --url) starts vite on 1444
- the run ends; stop() SIGTERMs the node pid
- per film-capture's own note, vite's children stay running
- fix: rig.mjs killTree(child) (taskkill /T on win32, SIGTERM elsewhere), used by ensureServer and film-capture

## Expected impact
Repeated rehearsal runs on the Windows dev box stop leaking processes. Risk: taskkill /F ends the server hard, as film-capture already does.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - no orphaned server processes after a takes run on Windows
Before: 2 server-stop implementations, 1 kills the tree (read of both files); orphan count on Windows not measured (needs a server run, out of this round)
After: predicted 0 orphans; measured by the instrument
Method: simulation - measuring needs starting vite, which this round may not do
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: Repeated rehearsal runs on the Windows dev box stop leaking processes. Risk: taskkill /F ends the server hard, as film-capture already does.
instrument: on Windows: ensureServer({port}) then stop(), and count processes whose ParentProcessId was the vite pid (Get-CimInstance Win32_Process) before/after; compare SIGTERM against taskkill /T
